title: Activation-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Sequence-Compressed Low-Rank Subspaces
abstract: arXiv:2604.22783v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has become the standard approach for adapting large language models (LLMs). However, despite reducing trainable parameter counts, many PEFT methods remain memory-bound by token-level activation intermediates that scale linearly with sequence length, limiting their practicality for long-context and on-device adaptation. Unlike prior memory-efficient PEFT approaches that preserve token-level adapter activations, LARS (Low-memory Activation-Rank Subspace) reduces the sequence-length scaling of stored adapter activation intermediates from O(BSRL) to O(BRL) by performing adaptation within a sequence-level low-rank subspace. Through pooled feature extraction, low-rank subspace modulations, and residual projection, LARS reduces the overall memory footprint by 23% on GPUs and 47.8% on CPUs relative to LoRA at S = 1024, with relative savings increasing with context length. Experiments across reason

translated_title: 通过序列压缩低秩子空间实现激活高效的微调
translated_abstract: 参数高效微调（PEFT）已成为适配大型语言模型（LLM）的标准方法。然而，尽管许多PEFT方法减少了可训练参数的数量，它们仍然受到随序列长度线性扩展的token级别激活中间量的内存限制，这限制了它们在长上下文和设备端适配场景中的实用性。与先前保留token级别适配器激活的记忆高效PEFT方法不同，LARS（低内存激活秩子空间）通过在序列级别的低秩子空间内执行适配，将存储的适配器激活中间量的序列长度扩展复杂度从O(BSRL)降低到O(BRL)。通过池化特征提取、低秩子空间调制和残差投影，LARS在S=1024时相比LoRA将总体内存占用在GPU上减少23%，在CPU上减少47.8%，且相对节省随上下文长度的增加而提升。实验在推理……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: LARS通过在序列级低秩子空间中执行适配，将存储的适配器激活中间量复杂度从O(BSRL)降至O(BRL)，相比LoRA在GPU和CPU上分别节省23%和47.8%的内存，且节省幅度随上下文长度增加而提升。
